## Concepts and intuitions {.unnumbered} -->

::: {style="margin-top: 1em; font-size: 125%; font-weight: 1000; text-align: center;"}
Ikotozafy ihany no Alexis!
:::

In the math subject, the most point rewarding is about the field problem, a function is given at the begining, then a series of questions like domaine def, studying derivative, etc. which culminates with drawing a plot of that function. But do you know that with most basic program you can just enter the function and it would plot the graph. So why is it a problem?

Obviously, there are educational purposes but by drilling too much, the pratical meaning is lost. Most, importantly, many becomes poor when a figure is presented in front of them. So for this, let's just go backward and attempt to link geometric properties to the analytical properties.

Later we will explore more general forms of functions @sec-functionCoding, but for the visualization, we will focus on the more familiar mathematical functions. A figure is the most powerful tool for to communicate ideas, improve literacy


## Formal {.unnumbered}
For simplicity, we look at X and Y as real number.
See for more details.
To graphically present a function, we need a few things
x axis to represent the value, we need a scale on that x axis.
y axis to represent the
The angle between x and y axis
The curve is just how y vary as we continuously change x

## Examples {.unnumbered}
The simplest is y = a*x + b and
to plot say a second degree polynomial, we could pick n values and plot each of them.
Well, this means that you can give any function and I can plot it.
With computer we can plot anything.

Come up with a fancier function, we are extracting the properties: definition, asymptote, derivative (sign), solution to equation, positive value

## Tips and warnings {.unnumbered}
- Linear function because it plots a line, pick two points and
- If x is discrete, you cannot just join line.
- Don't rush, project
- Changing scale can change quantitative visual (changing x axis)
- x = 0 intersection with, only one
- intersection with y = 0 are solution to f(x) = 0
- maximum, inflexion, minimum, increasing, decreasing, you can just look at that in the figure.
- Just plot and you are good to go.
- You can make figures with discrete x, see @sec-discrete_continuous, @sec-difference, @sec-pmf
